# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [mlatom/__init__.py](mlatom/__init__.py)

</details>



This document provides a comprehensive overview of MLatom, a package for atomistic simulations with machine learning. It covers the overall architecture, key capabilities, and how the different systems work together to enable ML-enhanced computational chemistry and molecular dynamics.

For specific installation and usage instructions, see [Getting Started](#1.1). For detailed information about individual subsystems, refer to the respective sections: [Core Architecture](#2), [Machine Learning Systems](#4), [Molecular Simulations](#5), and [Quantum Chemistry Interfaces](#6).

## Purpose and Scope

MLatom is an open-source package designed to integrate machine learning methods with atomistic simulations and quantum chemistry calculations. The package serves as a unified platform that combines:

- **Machine Learning Models**: Neural network potentials (ANI, MACE), kernel methods (KRR), and hybrid AI-QM approaches
- **Quantum Chemistry Interfaces**: Integration with major QM programs (PySCF, Gaussian, DFTB+, xTB)
- **Molecular Simulations**: Geometry optimization, frequency analysis, molecular dynamics, and nonadiabatic dynamics
- **Active Learning**: Automated model training and uncertainty quantification workflows
- **Spectroscopic Analysis**: UV/Vis, IR, and Raman spectra calculations

The package is distributed under an MIT license (modified to request proper citations) and is available both as a standalone Python package and through the XACS cloud computing platform.

Sources: [README.md:33-39](), [mlatom/__init__.py:1-16]()

## System Architecture

### High-Level Component Overview

MLatom follows a modular architecture with clear separation between user interface, task management, computational backends, and data handling layers.

#### System Architecture Diagram
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "User Interface Layer"
        MLatom_py["MLatom.py<br/>CLI Entry Point"]
        args_class_py["args_class.py<br/>Argument Parsing"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Management Core"
        MLtasks_py["MLtasks.py<br/>Task Orchestration"]
        data_py["data.py<br/>Core Data Structures"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ML and AI Systems"
        models_py["models.py<br/>Model Framework"]
        al_py["al.py<br/>Active Learning"]
        aiqm_methods["aiqm1.py + aiqm2.py<br/>AI-QM Methods"]
        ani_interface["torchani_interface.py<br/>ANI Models"]
        mace_interface["mace_interface.py<br/>MACE Models"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Quantum Chemistry Interfaces"
        pyscf_interface["pyscf_interface.py<br/>PySCF Integration"]
        gaussian_interface["gaussian_interface.py<br/>Gaussian Integration"]
        xtb_interface["xtb_interface.py<br/>xTB Integration"]
        dftbplus_interface["dftbplus_interface.py<br/>DFTB+ Integration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Simulation and Analysis"
        simulations_py["simulations.py<br/>Geometry Optimization & Frequencies"]
        namd_py["namd.py<br/>Nonadiabatic MD"]
        spectra_py["spectra.py<br/>Spectral Analysis"]
        md_cmd_py["md_cmd.py<br/>Molecular Dynamics"]
    end
    
    MLatom_py --> args_class_py
    MLatom_py --> MLtasks_py
    args_class_py --> MLtasks_py
    
    MLtasks_py --> data_py
    MLtasks_py --> models_py
    MLtasks_py --> simulations_py
    MLtasks_py --> al_py
    
    models_py --> ani_interface
    models_py --> mace_interface
    models_py --> aiqm_methods
    
    simulations_py --> pyscf_interface
    simulations_py --> gaussian_interface
    simulations_py --> xtb_interface
    simulations_py --> dftbplus_interface
    
    simulations_py --> namd_py
    simulations_py --> md_cmd_py
    data_py --> spectra_py
    
    al_py --> models_py
    al_py --> data_py
```

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:1-16]()

### Core Data Flow

The execution flow in MLatom follows a clear pipeline from user input to computational results:

#### Data Flow Pipeline
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CLI_Input["User Input<br/>(Command Line or Python API)"] --> MLatom_run["MLatom.run()<br/>Main Entry Point"]
    MLatom_run --> args_parsing["args_class<br/>Argument Parsing"]
    args_parsing --> task_dispatch["MLtasks<br/>Task Dispatch"]
    
    task_dispatch --> task_type{Task Type}
    
    task_type -->|"useMLmodel"| model_prediction["Model Prediction<br/>models.py"]
    task_type -->|"trainMLmodel"| model_training["Model Training<br/>models.py + al.py"]
    task_type -->|"geomopt"| geometry_opt["Geometry Optimization<br/>simulations.py"]
    task_type -->|"freq"| frequency_calc["Frequency Analysis<br/>simulations.py"]
    task_type -->|"md"| molecular_dynamics["Molecular Dynamics<br/>md_cmd.py"]
    task_type -->|"namd"| nonadiabatic_md["Nonadiabatic MD<br/>namd.py"]
    
    model_prediction --> method_selection["Method Selection"]
    model_training --> method_selection
    geometry_opt --> method_selection
    frequency_calc --> method_selection
    molecular_dynamics --> method_selection
    nonadiabatic_md --> method_selection
    
    method_selection --> method_type{Method Type}
    
    method_type -->|"ANI"| ani_calc["ANI Calculation<br/>torchani_interface.py"]
    method_type -->|"MACE"| mace_calc["MACE Calculation<br/>mace_interface.py"]
    method_type -->|"AIQM1/AIQM2"| aiqm_calc["AIQM Calculation<br/>aiqm1.py/aiqm2.py"]
    method_type -->|"PySCF"| pyscf_calc["PySCF Calculation<br/>pyscf_interface.py"]
    method_type -->|"Gaussian"| gaussian_calc["Gaussian Calculation<br/>gaussian_interface.py"]
    
    ani_calc --> data_processing["data.py<br/>Data Processing"]
    mace_calc --> data_processing
    aiqm_calc --> data_processing
    pyscf_calc --> data_processing
    gaussian_calc --> data_processing
    
    data_processing --> results["Results Output"]
```

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:2-3]()

## Key Capabilities

### Machine Learning Integration

MLatom provides extensive machine learning capabilities through several key components:

| Component | Purpose | Key Classes/Functions |
|-----------|---------|----------------------|
| **Model Framework** | Base infrastructure for ML models | `models.py`, `model_cls.py` |
| **Active Learning** | Automated model training with uncertainty | `al.py`, `al_utils.py` |
| **Neural Networks** | ANI, MACE, and custom NN potentials | `torchani_interface.py`, `mace_interface.py` |
| **Hybrid Methods** | AI-enhanced quantum methods | `aiqm1.py`, `aiqm2.py` |
| **Traditional ML** | Kernel ridge regression and related methods | `kreg` in `models.py` |

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:6-13]()

### Simulation Capabilities

The package supports a wide range of molecular simulation methods:

- **Geometry Optimization**: Single and multi-point optimizations with various optimizers
- **Frequency Analysis**: Vibrational frequencies, IR spectra, thermochemistry
- **Molecular Dynamics**: Classical MD with various thermostats and barostats  
- **Nonadiabatic Dynamics**: Surface hopping, trajectory calculations
- **Spectroscopic Analysis**: UV/Vis, IR, Raman spectra generation and analysis

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:4-5](), [README.md:13-19]()

### Quantum Chemistry Integration

MLatom interfaces with major quantum chemistry programs through dedicated modules:

- **PySCF**: DFT, post-HF methods, TDDFT calculations
- **Gaussian**: Full Gaussian functionality integration
- **DFTB+**: Density functional tight-binding calculations
- **xTB**: Extended tight-binding methods
- **Additional interfaces**: ORCA, Sparrow, MNDO, and others

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:7]()

## Entry Points and Usage

### Command Line Interface

The primary entry point is through the `MLatom.py` module, which provides the `run()` function:

```python
from mlatom import run
run()  # Command line interface
```

### Python API

Key classes and functions are directly importable:

```python
import mlatom
# Core data structures
mol = mlatom.molecule()
db = mlatom.molecular_database()

# Simulation functions  
mlatom.optimize_geometry(molecule=mol, method='AIQM1')
mlatom.freq(molecule=mol, method='AIQM1')

# Machine learning
model = mlatom.ani()
mlatom.al(molecular_database=db, model=model)
```

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:3-6]()

### Task-Based Execution

The `MLtasks` module orchestrates execution based on parsed arguments and task types, supporting both programmatic and CLI-driven workflows.

#### Task Execution Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
    user_input["User Input"] --> MLtasks_parse["MLtasks.parse()"]
    MLtasks_parse --> task_validation["Task Validation"]
    task_validation --> method_loading["Method Loading"]
    method_loading --> data_loading["Data Loading"]
    data_loading --> computation["Computation Execution"]
    computation --> results_output["Results Output"]
```

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:2]()

## Version and Updates

The current version is 3.18.3, with regular updates introducing new features such as:

- **Recent additions**: FSSH dynamics, KRR in Julia, MDtrajNet-1 model, ECTS diffusion model
- **Advanced features**: Multi-state ANI, gapMD, periodic boundary conditions
- **Enhanced interfaces**: Updated MACE support, improved QM program integration
- **Spectroscopy**: UV/Vis, IR, Raman spectra calculations with various methods

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:15](), [README.md:6-31]()

This overview provides the foundation for understanding MLatom's architecture and capabilities. For detailed information about specific subsystems, refer to the dedicated sections in this documentation.

# Page: Getting Started

# Getting Started

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [mlatom/MLatom.py](mlatom/MLatom.py)

</details>



This document covers the installation, basic usage patterns, and entry points for MLatom - a package for atomistic simulations with machine learning. This page provides the essential information needed to begin using MLatom effectively.

For detailed information about specific subsystems, see [Core Architecture](#2), [Machine Learning Systems](#4), [Molecular Simulations](#5), and [Quantum Chemistry Interfaces](#6).

## Installation and Setup

MLatom can be installed via pip using the following command:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -U MLatom
```

Additional dependencies may need to be installed depending on the specific features you plan to use. MLatom is distributed under an MIT license (modified to request proper citations) and is part of the XACS (Xiamen Atomistic Computing Suite).

### Version Management

MLatom provides built-in version management commands:

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `mlatom -v` or `mlatom --version` | Display current version and check for updates |
| `mlatom -l` or `mlatom --list` | List all available MLatom installations |

These commands are handled in the main entry point at [mlatom/MLatom.py:83-136]().

**Sources:** [README.md:41-45](), [mlatom/MLatom.py:83-136]()

## Basic Usage Patterns

### Command Line Execution

MLatom operates primarily through its command-line interface. The basic execution pattern follows this structure:

```bash
mlatom [options] [input_file]
```

### Execution Flow Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["User Command"] --> B["MLatom.py run()"]
    B --> C["Dynamic Module Loading"]
    C --> D["mlatom_args.parse()"]
    D --> E["header.printHeader()"]
    E --> F["CLItasks().run()"]
    F --> G["Task Execution"]
    G --> H["Results Output"]
    
    B --> I["Version Check (-v/--version)"]
    B --> J["Installation List (-l/--list)"]
```

**Entry Point Flow Diagram**

The system uses dynamic module loading to ensure the correct MLatom instance is loaded, particularly important when multiple versions may be installed.

**Sources:** [mlatom/MLatom.py:63-176]()

## System Entry Points

### Main Entry Point

The primary entry point is the `run()` function in [mlatom/MLatom.py:63](), which orchestrates the complete execution workflow:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Entry Point System"
        A["run() function"] --> B["Dynamic Module Loading"]
        B --> C["Argument Parsing"]
        C --> D["Header Display"]
        D --> E["Task Dispatch"]
        E --> F["Timing and Cleanup"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Components"
        G["mlatom_args"] --> C
        H["CLItasks"] --> E
        I["header module"] --> D
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Modes"
        J["Input File Mode"] --> C
        K["Direct Arguments"] --> C
        L["Version/List Mode"] --> A
    end
```

**Main System Components**

### Key System Components

| Component | File Location | Purpose |
|-----------|---------------|---------|
| `run()` | [mlatom/MLatom.py:63]() | Main execution orchestrator |
| `mlatom_args` | Referenced in [mlatom/MLatom.py:78]() | Command-line argument parsing |
| `CLItasks` | Referenced in [mlatom/MLatom.py:77]() | Task execution and dispatching |
| `header` | Referenced in [mlatom/MLatom.py:76]() | Version info and citations |

### Dynamic Module Loading

MLatom uses a sophisticated dynamic loading mechanism to ensure the correct instance is loaded:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as "User Command"
    participant M as "MLatom.py"
    participant I as "importlib.util"
    participant S as "sys.modules"
    
    U->>M: Execute mlatom command
    M->>M: Get directory path
    M->>I: spec_from_file_location()
    M->>I: module_from_spec()
    M->>S: Register module
    M->>I: exec_module()
    M->>M: Access components (header, CLItasks, etc.)
```

**Dynamic Loading Process**

This approach, implemented in [mlatom/MLatom.py:64-78](), handles cases where multiple MLatom versions might be installed and ensures consistent module loading.

**Sources:** [mlatom/MLatom.py:64-78]()

## Execution Workflow

### Standard Execution Process

The standard execution follows this sequence:

1. **Startup Phase**: Version display, argument parsing, and initialization
2. **Header Phase**: Citation information and system details 
3. **Task Phase**: Main computational work through `CLItasks`
4. **Cleanup Phase**: Timing information and termination

### Input Processing

MLatom supports two primary input modes:

| Mode | Description | Implementation |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| Input File | Single file containing all parameters | Detected in [mlatom/MLatom.py:147-154]() |
| Direct Arguments | Command-line arguments | Processed via `args.parse()` |

When an input file is provided, MLatom displays the file contents for transparency and reproducibility.

**Sources:** [mlatom/MLatom.py:140-172]()

## Next Steps

After successful installation and basic setup:

1. **Learn Core Concepts**: Review [Core Architecture](#2) for fundamental data structures and model framework
2. **Explore Tasks**: See [Command Line Interface](#3) for detailed argument handling and task types  
3. **Choose Application Area**:
   - Machine Learning: [Machine Learning Systems](#4)
   - Molecular Simulations: [Molecular Simulations](#5)
   - Quantum Chemistry: [Quantum Chemistry Interfaces](#6)

The system is designed with modularity in mind, allowing users to focus on specific capabilities while maintaining access to the full feature set through consistent interfaces.

**Sources:** [README.md:1-54](), [mlatom/MLatom.py:1-176]()

# Page: Core Architecture

# Core Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [mlatom/__init__.py](mlatom/__init__.py)
- [mlatom/data.py](mlatom/data.py)
- [mlatom/models.py](mlatom/models.py)

</details>



This document covers MLatom's fundamental data structures, model framework, and package organization that form the foundation for all molecular simulations and machine learning workflows. For command-line interface details, see [Command Line Interface](#3). For specific machine learning implementations, see [Machine Learning Systems](#4).

## Overview

MLatom's architecture is built around a hierarchy of core data structures and a flexible model framework that enables seamless integration between quantum chemistry calculations, machine learning models, and molecular simulations. The architecture follows a layered design where data flows from fundamental atomic representations through molecular assemblies to machine learning databases.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Core Data Layer"
        ATOM["atom<br/>Individual atomic data"]
        MOLECULE["molecule<br/>Collections of atoms<br/>+ properties"]
        MOLDB["molecular_database<br/>Collections of molecules"]
        MLDB["ml_database<br/>ML training data"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Framework"
        BASE["model (base class)"]
        MLMODEL["ml_model (base class)"]
        KRR["krr<br/>Kernel Ridge Regression"]
        KREG["kreg<br/>KREG implementation"]
        METHODS["methods()<br/>Universal model factory"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Layer"
        INTERFACES["Program Interfaces<br/>(ANI, MACE, Gaussian, etc.)"]
        TASKS["MLtasks.py<br/>Task orchestration"]
    end
    
    ATOM --> MOLECULE
    MOLECULE --> MOLDB
    MOLDB --> MLDB
    MLDB --> KRR
    MLDB --> KREG
    BASE --> MLMODEL
    MLMODEL --> KRR
    MLMODEL --> KREG
    METHODS --> KRR
    METHODS --> KREG
    METHODS --> INTERFACES
    TASKS --> MOLDB
    TASKS --> METHODS
```

Sources: [mlatom/data.py:1-2000](), [mlatom/models.py:1-800](), [mlatom/__init__.py:1-16]()

## Data Structure Hierarchy

The core data structures form a hierarchical system where atomic data aggregates into molecular representations, which then organize into databases for machine learning workflows.

### Atomic Level: `atom` Class

The `atom` class represents individual atoms with their nuclear properties and coordinates:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class atom {
        +atomic_number: int
        +element_symbol: str
        +nuclear_charge: int
        +nuclear_mass: float
        +xyz_coordinates: ndarray
        +copy() atom
    }
    class Properties {
        +multiplicity: float
        +H0: float 
        +nuclear_spin: float
    }
    atom --> Properties : "derived properties"
```

Key features include automatic element symbol resolution and isotope property lookup through the periodic table mapping system.

Sources: [mlatom/data.py:191-294]()

### Molecular Level: `molecule` Class

The `molecule` class aggregates atoms and manages molecular properties:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class molecule {
        +atoms: List[atom]
        +charge: int
        +multiplicity: int
        +xyz_coordinates: ndarray
        +electronic_states: List
        +pbc: ndarray
        +cell: ndarray
        +read_from_xyz_file()
        +copy() molecule
        +get_internuclear_distance_matrix()
    }
    class MolecularProperties {
        +energy: float
        +energy_gradients: ndarray
        +frequencies: ndarray
        +state_energies: ndarray
    }
    class GeometryOps {
        +bond_length()
        +bond_angle()
        +dihedral_angle()
        +proliferate()
    }
    molecule --> atom : "contains"
    molecule --> MolecularProperties : "stores"
    molecule --> GeometryOps : "geometry operations"
```

The class supports multiple file formats (XYZ, SMILES, Gaussian), periodic boundary conditions, and vectorial properties for gradients and forces.

Sources: [mlatom/data.py:329-1320]()

### Database Level: `molecular_database` and `ml_database`

Two complementary database classes handle different data organization needs:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "molecular_database"
        MOLDB_CLASS["molecular_database"]
        MOLS["molecules: List[molecule]"]
        MOLDB_OPS["read_from_xyz_file()<br/>read_from_h5_file()<br/>get_properties()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ml_database" 
        MLDB_CLASS["ml_database"]
        ENTRIES["entries: List[entry]"]
        ENTRY_CLASS["entry<br/>x: ndarray<br/>y: Union[float, ndarray]"]
        MLDB_OPS["split()<br/>get_x()<br/>get_property()"]
    end
    
    MOLDB_CLASS --> MOLS
    MOLDB_CLASS --> MOLDB_OPS
    MLDB_CLASS --> ENTRIES
    ENTRIES --> ENTRY_CLASS
    MLDB_CLASS --> MLDB_OPS
    
    MOLS -.-> ENTRIES : "can convert"
```

The `molecular_database` focuses on chemical structure and properties, while `ml_database` provides a general-purpose container for machine learning with arbitrary feature vectors and targets.

Sources: [mlatom/data.py:364-1600](), [mlatom/data.py:38-177]()

## Model Framework Architecture

The model framework provides a unified interface for various computational methods through an inheritance hierarchy and factory pattern.

### Base Model Classes

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class model {
        +predict()
        +parse_args()
        +generate_model_dict()
        +set_num_threads()
    }
    class ml_model {
        +train()
        +hyperparameters: hyperparameters
        +hyperparameter_optimization()
    }
    class OMP_model {
        +nthreads: int
    }
    class MKL_model {
        +nthreads: int
    }
    
    model <|-- ml_model
    ml_model <|-- OMP_model
    ml_model <|-- MKL_model
```

Base classes define common interfaces while specialized classes add training capabilities and threading support.

Sources: [mlatom/model_cls.py](), [mlatom/models.py:16-17]()

### Core ML Implementations

The framework includes two primary kernel-based implementations:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "KRR Implementation"
        KRR_CLASS["krr"]
        KRR_SCIPY["scipy backend"]
        KRR_JULIA["mlatom.jl backend"]
        KRR_KERNELS["Gaussian, Matern,<br/>periodic kernels"]
    end
    
    subgraph "KREG Implementation"
        KREG_CLASS["kreg"]
        KREG_API["KREG_API backend"]
        KREG_MLF["MLatomF backend"]
        KREG_DESC["RE descriptor<br/>generation"]
    end
    
    ml_model --> KRR_CLASS
    ml_model --> KREG_CLASS
    KRR_CLASS --> KRR_SCIPY
    KRR_CLASS --> KRR_JULIA
    KRR_CLASS --> KRR_KERNELS
    KREG_CLASS --> KREG_API
    KREG_CLASS --> KREG_MLF
    KREG_CLASS --> KREG_DESC
```

Both classes support energy and gradient predictions with automatic hyperparameter optimization capabilities.

Sources: [mlatom/models.py:18-342](), [mlatom/models.py:343-553]()

### Universal Method Factory

The `methods()` function provides a unified entry point for all computational methods:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["methods(method, program, **kwargs)"] --> B{program specified?}
    B -->|Yes| C["Load program-specific<br/>method class"]
    B -->|No| D["Search known_classes<br/>for method support"]
    
    C --> E["Return method instance"]
    D --> F{Method found?}
    F -->|Yes| E
    F -->|No| G["Raise ValueError"]
    
    H["known_classes list:<br/>aiqm1, aiqm2, ani_methods,<br/>gaussian_methods, pyscf_methods,<br/>etc."] --> D
```

This factory pattern enables automatic method detection and provides consistent interfaces across different quantum chemistry programs and ML models.

Sources: [mlatom/models.py:626-690](), [mlatom/models.py:624-625]()

## Package Organization

MLatom's modular structure separates concerns while enabling flexible composition:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Core Modules"
        DATA["data.py<br/>Fundamental data structures"]
        MODELS["models.py<br/>Model framework + implementations"]
        MODEL_CLS["model_cls.py<br/>Base classes"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Management"
        MLATOM["MLatom.py<br/>Main entry point"]
        MLTASKS["MLtasks.py<br/>Task orchestration"]
        ARGS["args_class.py<br/>Argument parsing"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Domain-Specific"
        SIM["simulations.py<br/>Molecular simulations"]
        AL["al.py<br/>Active learning"]
        NAMD["namd.py<br/>Nonadiabatic dynamics"]
        SPECTRA["spectra.py<br/>Spectroscopic analysis"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Interfaces"
        INTERFACES["interfaces/<br/>External program interfaces"]
    end
    
    MLATOM --> MLTASKS
    MLTASKS --> DATA
    MLTASKS --> MODELS
    MODELS --> MODEL_CLS
    MODELS --> INTERFACES
    SIM --> DATA
    AL --> MODELS
    NAMD --> SIM
```

The `__init__.py` exposes key classes and functions for direct user access while maintaining clean module boundaries.

Sources: [mlatom/__init__.py:1-16](), [mlatom/MLatom.py](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py]()

# Page: Data Structures

# Data Structures

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [mlatom/data.py](mlatom/data.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents the core data structures in MLatom that represent atoms, molecules, molecular databases, and trajectories. These classes form the foundation for all molecular data handling, from individual atomic properties to collections of molecules used in machine learning workflows and molecular dynamics simulations.

For information about the model framework that operates on these data structures, see [Model Framework](#2.2). For details about molecular simulations that generate trajectory data, see [Core Simulations](#5.1) and [Molecular Dynamics](#5.2).

## Core Atomic and Entry Structures

### Atom Class

The `atom` class [mlatom/data.py:191-294]() represents individual atoms with their fundamental properties:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class atom {
        +int atomic_number
        +str element_symbol
        +float nuclear_charge
        +float nuclear_mass
        +ndarray xyz_coordinates
        +property multiplicity
        +property H0
        +property nuclear_spin
        +copy() atom
    }
```

**Key Properties:**
- `atomic_number`: Defines the element type
- `element_symbol`: String representation (e.g., 'H', 'C', 'O')
- `xyz_coordinates`: 3D position in Angström units
- `nuclear_mass`: Atomic mass, with automatic isotope lookup

The class uses property decorators to provide multiple ways to access the same atomic information and automatically converts between atomic number, element symbol, and nuclear charge [mlatom/data.py:222-279]().

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:191-294]()

### Entry Class

The `entry` class [mlatom/data.py:23-37]() provides a basic data container for machine learning applications:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class entry {
        +str id
        +ndarray x
        +float|ndarray y
        +__add__(obj)
        +__str__()
    }
```

Each entry contains input features (`x`) and target values (`y`) with a unique identifier. Entries can be combined using the `+` operator to create `ml_database` objects.

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:23-37]()

## Molecular Structures

### Molecule Class

The `molecule` class [mlatom/data.py:329-1320]() is the central structure representing complete molecular systems:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class molecule {
        +str id
        +int charge
        +int multiplicity
        +List[atom] atoms
        +ndarray pbc
        +ndarray cell
        +List electronic_states
        +property atomic_numbers
        +property element_symbols
        +property xyz_coordinates
        +property energy_gradients
        +property kinetic_energy
        +from_xyz_file() molecule
        +from_numpy() molecule
        +from_smiles_string() molecule
        +copy() molecule
        +bond_length(a1, a2) float
        +bond_angle(a1, a2, a3) float
        +proliferate() molecule
    }
    molecule --> atom : contains
```

**Key Features:**
- **Atomic Structure**: Contains a list of `atom` objects
- **Electronic Properties**: Charge, multiplicity, electronic states
- **Periodic Boundary Conditions**: Support for periodic systems via `pbc` and `cell`
- **Multiple Input Formats**: Can be created from XYZ files, NumPy arrays, or SMILES strings
- **Geometric Analysis**: Built-in methods for bond lengths, angles, and dihedral angles

**Data Loading Methods:**
- `from_xyz_file()`: Standard XYZ format with support for COLUMBUS, NEWTON-X, and Turbomole formats
- `from_numpy()`: Direct creation from coordinate and species arrays
- `from_smiles_string()`: Generation from SMILES with 3D optimization

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:329-1320]()

## Database and Collection Structures

### Molecular Database

The `molecular_database` class [mlatom/data.py:1364-2239]() manages collections of molecules:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class molecular_database {
        +List[molecule] molecules
        +property size
        +property atomic_numbers
        +property xyz_coordinates
        +property energy
        +from_xyz_file() molecular_database
        +from_h5_file() molecular_database
        +read_from_numpy() molecular_database
        +add_scalar_properties()
        +add_xyz_derivative_properties()
        +split() List[molecular_database]
        +filter_by_property() molecular_database
        +groupby() List[molecular_database]
    }
    molecular_database --> molecule : contains
```

**Key Capabilities:**
- **Batch Operations**: Apply properties to all molecules simultaneously
- **Data Splitting**: Random or user-defined splits for training/validation
- **File I/O**: Support for XYZ, HDF5, JSON, and NPZ formats
- **Property Management**: Add scalar properties, gradients, and vectorial properties
- **Filtering and Grouping**: Select subsets based on property values

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:1364-2239]()

### ML Database

The `ml_database` class [mlatom/data.py:38-177]() is designed specifically for machine learning workflows:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ml_database {
        +List[entry] entries
        +property x
        +property y
        +property size
        +from_x_file() ml_database
        +read_from_y_file()
        +get_x() ndarray
        +get_property() ndarray
        +split() List[ml_database]
    }
    ml_database --> entry : contains
```

This class provides specialized methods for handling feature matrices (`x`) and target vectors (`y`) common in machine learning applications.

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:38-177]()

## Trajectory Structures

### Molecular Trajectory

For molecular dynamics and optimization tasks, MLatom provides trajectory data structures:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class molecular_trajectory {
        +List[molecular_trajectory_step] steps
        +dump(filename, format)
        +load(filename, format)
        +get_xyz_string() str
        +to_database() molecular_database
        +view()
    }
    class molecular_trajectory_step {
        +int step
        +molecule molecule
        +float time
        +ndarray state_coefficients
        +float random_number
        +List hopping_probabilities
    }
    molecular_trajectory --> molecular_trajectory_step : contains
    molecular_trajectory_step --> molecule : contains
```

**Supported Formats:**
- **H5MD**: High-performance binary format for large trajectories
- **JSON**: Human-readable format for smaller datasets
- **Plain Text**: Multiple files (XYZ, gradients, energies, etc.)

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:2561-2923]()

## Chemical Reaction Structures

MLatom provides specialized structures for handling chemical reactions:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class reaction {
        +List[reaction_step] steps
        +calculate_relative_energies()
    }
    class reaction_step {
        +List coefficients
        +List[molecule] molecules
        +str chemical_label
        +absolute_energy() float
        +copy() reaction_step
    }
    class reactions_database {
        +List[reaction] reactions
        +dump(filename, format)
        +load(filename, format)
        +groupby() List
    }
    reaction --> reaction_step : contains
    reaction_step --> molecule : contains
    reactions_database --> reaction : contains
```

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:2291-2436]()

## Data Flow and Relationships

The following diagram illustrates how data flows through MLatom's core structures:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Raw Input Files"] --> B["File Parsers"]
    B --> C["atom objects"]
    B --> D["entry objects"]
    
    C --> E["molecule objects"]
    D --> F["ml_database"]
    
    E --> G["molecular_database"]
    E --> H["molecular_trajectory_step"]
    
    H --> I["molecular_trajectory"]
    E --> J["reaction_step"]
    J --> K["reaction"]
    K --> L["reactions_database"]
    
    G --> M["ML Models & Simulations"]
    F --> M
    I --> M
    L --> M
    
    subgraph "File Formats"
        N["XYZ Files"]
        O["HDF5 Files"] 
        P["SMILES"]
        Q["JSON/NPZ"]
    end
    
    N --> B
    O --> B
    P --> B
    Q --> B
```

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:296-318](), [mlatom/data.py:436-564](), [mlatom/data.py:1405-1463]()

## Isotope and Atomic Data

MLatom includes comprehensive isotope data for accurate mass calculations:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class isotope {
        +int nuclear_charge
        +float relative_isotopic_mass
        +float isotope_abundance
        +float nuclear_spin
        +float H0
        +int multiplicity
    }
    class isotopes {
        +List[isotope] isotopes
        +get_most_abundant_with_given_nuclear_charge() isotope
        +get_most_similar_isotope_given_nuclear_charge_and_mass() isotope
    }
    isotopes --> isotope : contains
```

The isotope database contains data for elements 1-118 with nuclear masses, abundances, and nuclear spin information sourced from NIST [mlatom/data.py:3269-3665]().

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:3269-3665]()

## Utility and I/O Classes

### HDF5 Support

MLatom provides specialized HDF5 handling through several classes:

- `h5md`: H5MD format support for trajectory data [mlatom/data.py:2931-3080]()
- `h5dataloader`: Efficient loading of large HDF5 datasets [mlatom/data.py:3081-3130]()

### Data Conversion

The module includes utilities for converting between different data representations:
- `class_instance_to_dict()`: Serialization to dictionary format [mlatom/data.py:2439-2464]()
- `dict_to_*_class_instance()`: Deserialization from dictionaries [mlatom/data.py:2466-2559]()

**Sources:** [mlatom/data.py:2931-3130](), [mlatom/data.py:2439-2559]()

# Page: Model Framework

# Model Framework

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [mlatom/aiqm1.py](mlatom/aiqm1.py)
- [mlatom/aiqm2.py](mlatom/aiqm2.py)
- [mlatom/model_cls.py](mlatom/model_cls.py)
- [mlatom/models.py](mlatom/models.py)

</details>



This document covers the core model framework infrastructure in MLatom, including base model classes, kernel ridge regression (KRR/KREG) implementations, and model loading/saving mechanisms. The framework provides a unified interface for different types of computational models while handling threading, hyperparameter optimization, and model composition.

For information about specific machine learning implementations, see [Machine Learning Systems](#4). For quantum chemistry method interfaces, see [Quantum Chemistry Interfaces](#6).

## Base Model Classes Architecture

The model framework is built around a hierarchy of base classes that provide common functionality for all computational models in MLatom.

### Core Model Hierarchy

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class model {
        +nthreads: int
        +set_num_threads(nthreads)
        +predict(molecular_database, molecule, **kwargs)
        +dump(filename, format)
        +parse_args(args)
    }
    
    class torch_model {
        +set_num_threads(nthreads)
        +config_multiprocessing()
    }
    
    class torchani_model {
        +config_multiprocessing()
    }
    
    class tensorflow_model {
        +set_num_threads(nthreads)
    }
    
    class MKL_model {
        +set_num_threads(nthreads)
    }
    
    class OMP_model {
        +set_num_threads(nthreads)
    }
    
    class method_model {
        +is_method_supported(method)
        +is_program_found()
        +get_bin_env_var()
    }
    
    class ml_model {
        +train(molecular_database, property_to_learn)
        +predict(molecular_database, **kwargs)
        +optimize_hyperparameters()
        +calculate_validation_loss()
    }
    
    class downloadable_model {
        +check_model_path(model_dir, model_files)
        +download(download_links, target)
        +extract_zip(src, target)
    }
    
    model <|-- torch_model
    torch_model <|-- torchani_model
    model <|-- tensorflow_model
    model <|-- MKL_model
    model <|-- OMP_model
    model <|-- method_model
    model <|-- ml_model
    model <|-- downloadable_model
```

The base `model` class [mlatom/model_cls.py:20-131]() provides fundamental functionality including:
- Thread management via `set_num_threads()`
- Universal prediction interface through `predict()`
- Model serialization with `dump()`
- Integration with geometry optimization logging

Specialized base classes handle different computational backends:
- `torch_model` [mlatom/model_cls.py:132-144]() manages PyTorch threading
- `tensorflow_model` [mlatom/model_cls.py:150-155]() sets TensorFlow parallelism
- `MKL_model` and `OMP_model` [mlatom/model_cls.py:156-167]() control Intel MKL and OpenMP threads

**Sources:** [mlatom/model_cls.py:20-200]()

### Method and Model Discovery

The `method_model` class [mlatom/model_cls.py:168-200]() provides automatic method discovery:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["methods(method='AIQM1')"] --> B["method_model.is_method_supported()"]
    B --> C{Method in supported_methods?}
    C -->|Yes| D["method_model.is_program_found()"]
    C -->|No| E["Try next known_class"]
    D --> F{Binary found via bin_env_name?}
    F -->|Yes| G["Return method instance"]
    F -->|No| E
    E --> H["Raise ValueError"]
```

The `known_classes` list [mlatom/models.py:624]() defines the search order for method resolution, with AIQM methods having priority over basic quantum chemistry interfaces.

**Sources:** [mlatom/model_cls.py:168-200](), [mlatom/models.py:626-691]()

## KRR/KREG Implementations

### Kernel Ridge Regression Architecture

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class krr {
        +ml_program: str
        +kernel_function: str
        +hyperparameters: hyperparameters
        +train(molecular_database, property_to_learn)
        +predict(molecular_database, **kwargs)
        +gaussian_kernel_function()
    }
    
    class kreg {
        +equilibrium_molecule: molecule
        +get_descriptor(molecular_database)
        +get_equilibrium_distances()
        +train(molecular_database, **kwargs)
        +predict(molecular_database, **kwargs)
    }
    
    class KREG_API {
        +train()
        +predict()
        +save_model()
        +load_model()
    }
    
    class KRR_julia {
        +train()
        +predict()
        +save_model()
        +load_model()
    }
    
    ml_model <|-- krr
    krr <|-- kreg
    OMP_model <|-- kreg
    MKL_model <|-- kreg
    kreg --> KREG_API
    krr --> KRR_julia
```

The `krr` class [mlatom/models.py:18-342]() implements kernel ridge regression with multiple backend options:
- `scipy` backend for direct matrix operations
- `mlatom.jl` backend using Julia implementation

Key features include:
- Multiple kernel functions: Gaussian, periodic Gaussian, Matern
- Automatic hyperparameter initialization based on kernel type
- Support for training on both energies and gradients

**Sources:** [mlatom/models.py:18-342]()

### KREG Implementation Details

The `kreg` class [mlatom/models.py:343-553]() extends KRR with relative equilibrium (RE) descriptors:

```python
# Descriptor calculation using equilibrium distances
descriptor[ii] = eq_distmat[iatomind][jatomind]/distmat[iatomind][jatomind]
```

The class supports two primary backends:
- `KREG_API` for optimized native implementation
- `MLatomF` for legacy Fortran interface

Training workflow [mlatom/models.py:459-521]():
1. Determine equilibrium molecule from lowest energy structure
2. Generate RE descriptors for all molecules  
3. Train kernel matrix with regularization
4. Save model coefficients

**Sources:** [mlatom/models.py:343-553]()

## Model Factory and Loading System

### Method Factory Function

The `methods()` function [mlatom/models.py:626-691]() serves as the primary entry point for model creation:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["methods(method, program, **kwargs)"] --> B{program specified?}
    B -->|Yes| C["Use program_methods module"]
    B -->|No| D["Search known_classes"]
    
    C --> E["program_methods(method, **kwargs)"]
    D --> F["For each method_class in known_classes"]
    F --> G{is_method_supported(method)?}
    G -->|Yes| H{is_program_found()?}
    G -->|No| I["Try next class"]
    H -->|Yes| J["method_class(method, **kwargs)"]
    H -->|No| I
    I --> K{More classes?}
    K -->|Yes| F
    K -->|No| L["Raise ValueError"]
```

The factory supports both explicit program specification and automatic discovery based on available programs and supported methods.

**Sources:** [mlatom/models.py:626-691]()

### Model Loading Infrastructure

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["load(filename, format)"] --> B{format == 'json'?}
    B -->|Yes| C["load_json(filename)"]
    B -->|No| D["load_pickle(filename)"]
    
    C --> E["json.load() → model_dict"]
    D --> F["pickle.load()"]
    
    E --> G["load_dict(model_dict)"]
    G --> H{type == 'method'?}
    H -->|Yes| I["methods(**model_dict)"]
    H -->|No| J{type == 'ml_model'?}
    J -->|Yes| K["globals()[ml_model_type](**kwargs)"]
    J -->|No| L{type == 'model_tree_node'?}
    L -->|Yes| M["Reconstruct tree recursively"]
    L -->|No| N["import_from_path() + dynamic instantiation"]
```

Model serialization preserves:
- Model type and module information
- Hyperparameter values and constraints  
- Thread configuration
- Nested model structures for composite models

**Sources:** [mlatom/models.py:699-773]()

## Hyperparameter Management

### Hyperparameter Classes

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class hyperparameter {
        +value: Any
        +optimization_space: str
        +dtype: Callable
        +minval: Any
        +maxval: Any
        +step: Any
        +choices: Iterable
        +update(new_hyperparameter)
        +copy()
    }
    
    class hyperparameters {
        +data: dict
        +__setitem__(key, value)
        +__getattr__(key)
        +copy(keys)
    }
    
    UserDict <|-- hyperparameters
    hyperparameters --> hyperparameter
```

The `hyperparameter` class [mlatom/model_cls.py:849-898]() encapsulates individual parameters with:
- Value storage with automatic type casting
- Optimization space definition (linear, log, etc.)
- Bounds and constraints for optimization

The `hyperparameters` class [mlatom/model_cls.py:900-951]() provides a dictionary-like interface with automatic conversion to `hyperparameter` objects.

**Sources:** [mlatom/model_cls.py:849-951]()

### Hyperparameter Optimization

The `ml_model.optimize_hyperparameters()` method [mlatom/model_cls.py:602-721]() supports multiple optimization algorithms:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["optimize_hyperparameters()"] --> B{optimization_algorithm}
    B -->|"grid"| C["Grid search with scipy.optimize"]
    B -->|"TPE"| D["Tree-structured Parzen Estimator with hyperopt"]
    B -->|"Nelder-Mead"| E["Scipy minimize methods"]
    B -->|"BFGS", "L-BFGS-B", etc.| E
    
    C --> F["optimize_grid() custom implementation"]
    D --> G["hyperopt.fmin() with space mapping"]
    E --> H["scipy.optimize.minimize()"]
    
    F --> I["Update hyperparameters.value"]
    G --> I
    H --> I
```

Cross-validation and holdout validation are handled through `cross_validation()` and `holdout_validation()` methods that automatically split datasets and calculate validation losses.

**Sources:** [mlatom/model_cls.py:602-764]()

## Model Composition System

### Model Tree Node Architecture

The `model_tree_node` class [mlatom/model_cls.py:953-1135]() enables hierarchical model composition:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class model_tree_node {
        +name: str
        +parent: model_tree_node
        +children: List[model_tree_node]
        +operator: str
        +model: model
        +weight: float
        +predict(**kwargs)
        +set_num_threads(nthreads)
        +dump(filename, format)
    }
    
    class data.properties_tree_node {
        +name: str
        +parent: properties_tree_node
        +children: List[properties_tree_node]
        +sum(properties)
        +average(properties)
        +weighted_sum(properties)
    }
    
    model <|-- model_tree_node
    model_tree_node --> data.properties_tree_node
```

Supported operators [mlatom/model_cls.py:1057-1074]():
- `predict`: Execute child model prediction
- `sum`: Add results from all children  
- `average`: Compute mean of child results
- `weighted_sum`: Weighted combination using node weights

**Sources:** [mlatom/model_cls.py:953-1135]()

### Example: AIQM1 Model Composition

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["aiqm1_model"] --> B["aiqm1_nn (average)"]
    A --> C["aiqm1_atomic_energy_shift (predict)"]
    A --> D["odm2star (predict)"]
    A --> E["d4_wb97x (predict)"]
    
    B --> F["aiqm1_nn0 (predict)"]
    B --> G["aiqm1_nn1 (predict)"]
    B --> H["... (predict)"]
    B --> I["aiqm1_nn7 (predict)"]
    
    F --> J["ani_nns_in_aiqm1(model_index=0)"]
    G --> K["ani_nns_in_aiqm1(model_index=1)"]
    I --> L["ani_nns_in_aiqm1(model_index=7)"]
```

This composition [mlatom/aiqm1.py:54-66]() combines:
- 8 neural network models (averaged)
- Atomic energy shift corrections
- ODM2* quantum mechanical method
- D4 dispersion corrections

The tree structure automatically handles property aggregation and uncertainty quantification across all component models.

**Sources:** [mlatom/aiqm1.py:54-66](), [mlatom/model_cls.py:987-1077]()

# Page: Command Line Interface

# Command Line Interface

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [mlatom/MLatom.py](mlatom/MLatom.py)
- [mlatom/MLtasks.py](mlatom/MLtasks.py)
- [mlatom/args_class.py](mlatom/args_class.py)
- [mlatom/interfaces/xtb_interface.py](mlatom/interfaces/xtb_interface.py)

</details>



The Command Line Interface (CLI) is the primary entry point for users to interact with MLatom. It provides a unified command-line interface that handles argument parsing, task dispatching, and execution flow control for all MLatom functionality including machine learning tasks, molecular simulations, and quantum chemistry calculations.

For information about the core task implementations, see [Task Management and Arguments](#3.2). For details on the underlying data structures used by CLI tasks, see [Data Structures](#2.1).

## CLI Architecture Overview

The MLatom CLI follows a three-layer architecture that separates user input processing, argument parsing, and task execution:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "User Interface Layer"
        CLI["`MLatom.py
        Main Entry Point`"]
        VERSION["`Version Check
        -v, --version`"]
        LIST["`Installation List
        -l, --list`"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Argument Processing Layer"  
        ARGS["`args_class.py
        mlatom_args`"]
        PARSE["`Argument Parsing
        File & CLI Args`"]
        VALID["`Argument Validation
        Task & Method Detection`"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task Execution Layer"
        DISPATCH["`MLtasks.py
        CLItasks`"]
        MLATOMF["`MLatomF Interface
        Legacy Tasks`"]
        TASKS["`Python Task Functions
        Modern Implementation`"]
    end
    
    CLI --> VERSION
    CLI --> LIST  
    CLI --> ARGS
    ARGS --> PARSE
    PARSE --> VALID
    VALID --> DISPATCH
    DISPATCH --> MLATOMF
    DISPATCH --> TASKS
```

**CLI Entry Point Flow**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:63-173](), [mlatom/args_class.py:401-762](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:14-29]()

## Command Line Execution Flow

The CLI execution follows a structured pipeline from user input to task completion:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["`User Command
    mlatom [options] or [file]`"] --> ENTRY["`run() function
    MLatom.py:63`"]
    
    ENTRY --> CHECK{"`Special Flags?`"}
    CHECK -->|"-v, --version"| VER["`Version Display
    MLatom.py:84-98`"]
    CHECK -->|"-l, --list"| LST["`Installation List
    MLatom.py:99-136`"]
    CHECK -->|"No"| LOAD["`Dynamic Module Loading
    MLatom.py:64-78`"]
    
    LOAD --> PARSE["`mlatom_args.parse()
    args_class.py:645-655`"]
    PARSE --> VALIDATE["`Argument Validation
    args_class.py:695-738`"]
    VALIDATE --> DISPATCH["`CLItasks(args).run()
    MLtasks.py:25-29`"]
    
    DISPATCH --> ROUTE{"`Task Type?`"}
    ROUTE -->|"MLatomF Compatible"| MLF["`run_with_mlatomF()
    MLtasks.py:31-40`"]
    ROUTE -->|"Python Implementation"| PY["`Python Task Function
    MLtasks.py:43+`"]
    
    MLF --> RESULT["`Task Results`"]
    PY --> RESULT
    RESULT --> TIMING["`Wall-clock Timing
    MLatom.py:166-171`"]
    
    VER --> EXIT["`Program Exit`"]
    LST --> EXIT
    TIMING --> EXIT
```

**Command Execution Pipeline**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:63-173](), [mlatom/args_class.py:645-655](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:25-40]()

## Task Categories and Dispatch

MLatom organizes functionality into distinct task categories, each handled by specific dispatch logic:

| Category | Tasks | Handler |
|----------|-------|---------|
| ML Tasks | `useMLmodel`, `createMLmodel`, `estAccMLmodel` | Python or MLatomF |
| Data Tasks | `XYZ2X`, `analyze`, `sample` | Mixed implementation |
| Simulation Tasks | `geomopt`, `freq`, `MD`, `al` | Python implementation |
| Specialized | `learningCurve`, `crossSection`, `MLQD` | Python implementation |

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Task Dispatch Logic"
        CLITASKS["`CLItasks.__init__()
        MLtasks.py:23-24`"]
        RUN["`CLItasks.run()
        MLtasks.py:25-29`"]
        CHECK{"`MLatomF Compatible?
        MLtasks.py:26`"}
    end
    
    subgraph "MLatomF Tasks"
        MLF_LIST["`MLatomF_tasks
        ['useMLmodel', 'createMLmodel', 
         'estAccMLmodel', 'XYZ2X', 
         'analize', 'sample']`"]
        MLF_RUN["`run_with_mlatomF()
        MLtasks.py:31-40`"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Python Tasks"
        PY_TASKS["`Python Task Functions
        useMLmodel(), createMLmodel(),
        geomopt(), freq(), MD(), etc.`"]
        GLOBALS["`globals()[task]()
        MLtasks.py:29`"]
    end
    
    CLITASKS --> RUN
    RUN --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|"Yes & Conditions Met"| MLF_LIST
    CHECK -->|"No"| GLOBALS
    MLF_LIST --> MLF_RUN
    GLOBALS --> PY_TASKS
```

**Task Dispatch Architecture**
Sources: [mlatom/MLtasks.py:14-29](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:31-40]()

## Dynamic Module Loading

MLatom implements sophisticated dynamic module loading to ensure that the CLI uses the same instance of the mlatom package from which it's executed:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as "User"
    participant CLI as "MLatom.py run()"
    participant IMP as "importlib.util" 
    participant MOD as "mlatom module"
    participant SYS as "sys.modules"
    
    U->>CLI: "Execute mlatom command"
    CLI->>CLI: "Get directory path of __file__"
    CLI->>IMP: "spec_from_file_location(dirname, path2init)"
    IMP->>CLI: "Return module spec"
    CLI->>IMP: "module_from_spec(spec)"
    IMP->>CLI: "Return module object"
    CLI->>SYS: "sys.modules[dirname] = module"
    CLI->>IMP: "spec.loader.exec_module(module)"
    IMP->>MOD: "Load module components"
    CLI->>CLI: "Extract header, CLItasks, mlatom_args"
```

**Dynamic Loading Sequence**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:64-78]()

## Version and Installation Management

The CLI provides built-in version checking and installation discovery capabilities:

| Flag | Function | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| `-v`, `--version` | Version display | Shows current version, checks for updates |
| `-l`, `--list` | Installation list | Lists all available MLatom installations |

The version checking system [mlatom/MLatom.py:84-98]() queries PyPI for the latest version and notifies users of available updates. The installation listing system [mlatom/MLatom.py:99-136]() searches multiple locations including:

- Current installation directory
- PYTHONPATH directories  
- Site-packages directories

Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:84-136]()

# Page: Entry Point and Execution

# Entry Point and Execution

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [mlatom/MLatom.py](mlatom/MLatom.py)

</details>



This document covers the main entry point and execution control mechanisms in MLatom, specifically focusing on the command-line interface entry point and how execution flows through the system. This includes dynamic module loading, version management, argument parsing integration, and task execution orchestration.

For information about specific task implementations and argument parsing details, see [Task Management and Arguments](#3.2). For details about the core data structures used during execution, see [Data Structures](#2.1).

## Main Entry Point Function

The primary entry point for MLatom is the `run()` function in [mlatom/MLatom.py:63-173](). This function serves as both the programmatic API entry point and the command-line interface handler.

The `run()` function accepts an optional `argv` parameter, allowing it to be called either:
- Directly from the command line (using `sys.argv`)
- Programmatically with custom arguments

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["run(argv=[])"] --> B{"argv empty?"}
    B -->|Yes| C["args.parse(sys.argv[1:])"]
    B -->|No| D["args.parse(argv)"]
    C --> E["CLItasks(args).run()"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["Return result"]
```

**Main Entry Point Flow**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:63-173]()

## Dynamic Module Loading

MLatom implements a sophisticated dynamic module loading mechanism to ensure that the correct instance of the mlatom package is used, particularly important when multiple versions might be installed.

The loading process involves several key steps:

| Step | Action | Code Location |
|------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | Get directory path of current file | [mlatom/MLatom.py:69]() |
| 2 | Build path to `__init__.py` | [mlatom/MLatom.py:70]() |
| 3 | Create module spec from file location | [mlatom/MLatom.py:72-73]() |
| 4 | Load module and register in `sys.modules` | [mlatom/MLatom.py:74-75]() |
| 5 | Import required submodules | [mlatom/MLatom.py:76-78]() |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["run() called"] --> B["os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))"]
    B --> C["path2init = os.path.join(dir_path, '__init__.py')"]
    C --> D["importlib.util.spec_from_file_location()"]
    D --> E["importlib.util.module_from_spec()"]
    E --> F["sys.modules[dirname] = module"]
    F --> G["spec.loader.exec_module()"]
    G --> H["Extract: header, CLItasks, mlatom_args"]
    H --> I["Continue execution with loaded modules"]
```

**Dynamic Module Loading Process**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:64-78]()

## Version Management

The entry point provides comprehensive version management functionality through command-line flags:

### Version Display (`-v`, `--version`)

When the version flag is provided, the system:
1. Displays the current version from `mlatom_with_this_file.__version__`
2. Checks PyPI for the latest version (if not a development version)
3. Suggests upgrade if a newer version is available

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Version flag detected"] --> B["Print current version"]
    B --> C{"Development version?"}
    C -->|No| D["Request PyPI API"]
    C -->|Yes| E["Exit"]
    D --> F{"Response OK?"}
    F -->|Yes| G["Compare versions"]
    F -->|No| H["Print error message"]
    G --> I{"Newer available?"}
    I -->|Yes| J["Suggest upgrade"]
    I -->|No| E
    J --> E
    H --> E
```

**Version Check Flow**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:83-98]()

### Installation Listing (`-l`, `--list`)

The list functionality discovers all MLatom installations by searching:
- Current installation location
- `PYTHONPATH` directories
- Site packages directories

The search process uses the helper function `get_version_from_init()` to extract version information from `__init__.py` files.

Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:99-136]()

## Execution Flow

The main execution sequence follows a structured pattern with comprehensive logging and timing:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Start execution"] --> B["Record start time"]
    B --> C["Print header and options"]
    C --> D["Check for input file"]
    D --> E{"Single file argument?"}
    E -->|Yes| F["Display file contents"]
    E -->|No| G["Continue"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["Create mlatom_args()"]
    H --> I["Parse arguments"]
    I --> J["Print header with args"]
    J --> K["Execute CLItasks(args).run()"]
    K --> L["Calculate wall-clock time"]
    L --> M["Print timing information"]
    M --> N["Return result"]
```

**Main Execution Flow**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:80-173]()

### Output Formatting

The entry point provides consistent output formatting with:
- Header sections delimited by `=` characters (78 characters wide)
- Timestamp logging for start and end times
- Wall-clock time reporting in seconds, minutes, and hours
- Input file content display for single-file inputs

Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:138-155](), [mlatom/MLatom.py:166-171]()

## Integration with Core Systems

The entry point serves as the orchestration layer connecting several core systems:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["MLatom.py run()"] --> B["Dynamic Module Loading"]
    B --> C["header module"]
    B --> D["CLItasks class"]
    B --> E["mlatom_args class"]
    
    C --> F["printHeader(args)"]
    D --> G["CLItasks(args).run()"]
    E --> H["args.parse()"]
    
    F --> I["Task Execution"]
    G --> I
    H --> I
    
    I --> J["Result Processing"]
```

**System Integration Architecture**
Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:76-78](), [mlatom/MLatom.py:155-164]()

### Component Responsibilities

| Component | Responsibility | Integration Point |
|-----------|----------------|-------------------|
| `header` | Version info and citation printing | [mlatom/MLatom.py:76](), [mlatom/MLatom.py:161]() |
| `CLItasks` | Task execution and orchestration | [mlatom/MLatom.py:77](), [mlatom/MLatom.py:164]() |
| `mlatom_args` | Command-line argument parsing | [mlatom/MLatom.py:78](), [mlatom/MLatom.py:155-159]() |

The entry point maintains a clean separation of concerns while providing unified access to all MLatom functionality through the command-line interface.

Sources: [mlatom/MLatom.py:63-173]()

# Page: Task Management and Arguments

# Task Management and Arguments

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [mlatom/MLtasks.py](mlatom/MLtasks.py)
- [mlatom/args_class.py](mlatom/args_class.py)
- [mlatom/interfaces/xtb_interface.py](mlatom/interfaces/xtb_interface.py)

</details>



This page documents MLatom's command-line interface task management and argument parsing system. It covers how user input is parsed, validated, and dispatched to appropriate task implementations. For information about the main entry point and execution flow, see [Entry Point and Execution](#3.1).

## Architecture Overview

The CLI system consists of two main components: argument parsing handled by the `mlatom_args` class, and task dispatch managed by the `CLItasks` class. The system supports both legacy Fortran implementations (MLatomF) and modern Python implementations for various computational tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["User Input"] --> B["mlatom_args.parse()"]
    B --> C["Argument Validation"]
    C --> D["Task Identification"]
    D --> E["CLItasks.run()"]
    E --> F{{"Task Route Decision"}}
    F -->|"MLatomF Compatible"| G["run_with_mlatomF()"]
    F -->|"Python Implementation"| H["Task Function"]
    G --> I["interface_MLatomF.run()"]
    H --> J["Task-Specific Logic"]
    I --> K["Results"]
    J --> K
```

Sources: [mlatom/args_class.py:645-656](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:25-29](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:31-40]()

## Argument Parsing System

### Core Classes

The argument parsing is built on a hierarchical class structure with specialized handling for MLatom's diverse parameter set:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ArgsBase {
        +data: AttributeDict
        +add_default_dict_args()
        +parse_input_content()
        +args_string_list()
        +_multi_level_dict()
    }
    
    class mlatom_args {
        +_task_list: List[str]
        +_method_list: List[str] 
        +parse(argsraw)
        +_checkArgs()
        +_check_hyperopt()
        +task: str
        +args2pass: List[str]
    }
    
    class AttributeDict {
        +lower_key_set: Set
        +lower_key_to_key: Dict
        +merge_dict()
        +key_in_dict()
    }
    
    ArgsBase <|-- mlatom_args
    ArgsBase --> AttributeDict
```

Sources: [mlatom/args_class.py:153-172](), [mlatom/args_class.py:401-407](), [mlatom/args_class.py:53-62]()

### Supported Tasks and Methods

The system defines comprehensive lists of supported computational tasks and quantum chemistry methods:

| Task Category | Examples | Implementation |
|---------------|----------|----------------|
| ML Tasks | `useMLmodel`, `createMLmodel`, `estAccMLmodel` | Python/MLatomF |
| Data Tasks | `XYZ2SMI`, `sample`, `analyze` | Mixed |
| Simulation Tasks | `geomopt`, `freq`, `MD`, `irc` | Python |
| Analysis Tasks | `crossSection`, `MLQD`, `al` | Python |

Sources: [mlatom/args_class.py:410-437](), [mlatom/args_class.py:444]()

### Argument Processing Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as "User Input"
    participant P as "mlatom_args.parse()"
    participant V as "_checkArgs()"
    participant H as "_check_hyperopt()" 
    participant T as "Task Dispatcher"
    
    U->>P: Raw arguments
    P->>P: parse_input_content()
    P->>V: Validate arguments
    V->>V: Identify task
    V->>V: Set method flags
    P->>H: Process hyperparameters
    P->>T: Validated args
```

Sources: [mlatom/args_class.py:645-656](), [mlatom/args_class.py:695-738](), [mlatom/args_class.py:680-693]()

## Task Dispatch Mechanism

### CLItasks Class

The `CLItasks` class serves as the central dispatcher, routing tasks between MLatomF (Fortran) and Python implementations based on compatibility and feature requirements:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["CLItasks.__init__(args)"] --> B["CLItasks.run()"]
    B --> C{{"Check MLatomF Compatibility"}}
    C -->|"Compatible Task"| D["run_with_mlatomF()"]
    C -->|"Python Only"| E["globals()[task](args)"]
    D --> F["interface_MLatomF.run()"]
    E --> G["Task Function Call"]
    
    H["MLatomF_tasks List"] --> C
    I["Method Checks"] --> C
    J["Hyperopt Checks"] --> C
```

Sources: [mlatom/MLtasks.py:14-29](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:15-22]()

### Task Implementation Categories

The system implements tasks through several patterns:

| Pattern | Examples | Description |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| Direct Functions | `useMLmodel()`, `createMLmodel()` | Core ML workflow tasks |
| Simulation Tasks | `geomopt()`, `freq()`, `MD()` | Molecular simulation workflows |
| Data Processing | `XYZ2SMI()`, `sample()` | File format conversion and sampling |
| Interface Wrappers | `al()`, `MLQD()` | Calls to specialized modules |

Sources: [mlatom/MLtasks.py:43-651]()

## Key Task Functions

### Machine Learning Tasks

The core ML tasks follow a consistent pattern of data loading, model setup, and execution:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["useMLmodel(args)"] --> B["loading_data()"]
    B --> C["loading_model()"]
    C --> D["predicting()"]
    D --> E["saving_predictions()"]
    
    F["createMLmodel(args)"] --> G["loading_data()"]
    G --> H["sampling()"]
    H --> I["loading_model()"]
    I --> J["training()"]
    
    K["estAccMLmodel(args)"] --> L["Cross-validation Logic"]
    L --> M["training() + predicting()"]
    M --> N["analyzing()"]
```

Sources: [mlatom/MLtasks.py:43-77](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:79-93](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:95-148]()

### Reusable Utility Functions

The system provides several reusable functions that support multiple tasks:

| Function | Purpose | Key Parameters |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| `loading_data()` | Load molecular databases from files | `XYZfile`, `Yfile`, `YgradXYZfile` |
| `loading_model()` | Instantiate ML models or methods | `MLprog`, `method`, `MLmodelIn` |
| `sampling()` | Generate train/test splits | `sampling`, `Ntrain`, `CVtest` |
| `predicting()` | Run model predictions | `value`, `gradient`, `hessian` |
| `analyzing()` | Compute statistical metrics | `ref_value`, `est_value` |

Sources: [mlatom/MLtasks.py:653-666](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:693-717](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:719-825](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:827-844](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:887-1013]()

## Integration with Model Framework

The task system integrates with MLatom's model framework through standardized interfaces:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Task Function"] --> B["loading_model(args)"]
    B --> C{{"Method vs ML Model"}}
    C -->|"Method"| D["loading_method()"]
    C -->|"ML Model"| E["Model Class Factory"]
    D --> F["models.methods()"]
    E --> G["models.kreg/ani/mace/etc"]
    F --> H["QM Interface"]
    G --> I["ML Interface"]
    
    J["args.method"] --> D
    K["args.MLprog"] --> E
    L["args.MLmodelIn"] --> E
```

Sources: [mlatom/MLtasks.py:693-717](), [mlatom/MLtasks.py:668-691]()

## Error Handling and Validation

The argument validation system performs several checks to ensure proper task execution:

### Task Detection Logic

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["_checkArgs()"] --> B{{"Count Active Tasks"}}
    B -->|"One Task"| C["Set _task"]
    B -->|"Multiple Tasks"| D{{"Special Combinations?"}}
    B -->|"No Tasks"| E{{"Method Specified?"}}
    
    D -->|"selfCorrect"| F["task = 'selfCorrect'"]
    D -->|"geomopt + freq"| G["task = 'optfreq'"]
    D -->|"ts + freq"| H["task = 'tsfreq'"]
    D -->|"Other"| I["Use First Task"]
    
    E -->|"Yes"| J["task = 'useMLmodel'"]
    E -->|"No"| K["Print Help & Exit"]
```

Sources: [mlatom/args_class.py:695-738]()

### Hyperparameter Optimization Setup

The system automatically detects and configures hyperparameter optimization based on argument patterns:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["_check_hyperopt()"] --> B["Scan args2pass"]
    B --> C{{"Find 'hyperopt.x(...)' pattern?"}}
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Extract hyperparameters"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Standard execution"]
    D --> F["Set optimization_algorithm"]
    F --> G["Build hyperparameter_optimization dict"]
```

Sources: [mlatom/args_class.py:680-693]()

This architecture provides a flexible and extensible system for managing diverse computational chemistry tasks while maintaining compatibility with legacy components and supporting advanced features like hyperparameter optimization and cross-validation.

# Page: Machine Learning Systems

# Machine Learning Systems

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This page documents MLatom's machine learning capabilities, including active learning workflows, neural network models, and AI-enhanced quantum mechanical methods. The ML systems provide automated model training, uncertainty quantification, and hybrid AI-QM approaches for molecular simulations.

For quantum chemistry interfaces that these ML models can interface with, see [Quantum Chemistry Interfaces](#6). For core data structures used by ML models, see [Data Structures](#2.1). For the overall model framework architecture, see [Model Framework](#2.2).

## Architecture Overview

The machine learning systems in MLatom are built around several core components that work together to provide comprehensive ML-driven molecular modeling capabilities.

**ML System Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TB

    subgraph "Base Framework"

    end
```

## Active Learning System

The active learning system automates the iterative process of training ML models, sampling new points based on uncertainty, and retraining models with expanded datasets.

### Core Active Learning Workflow

The main active learning class `al` orchestrates the entire workflow:

| Component | Class/Function | Description |
|-----------|----------------|-------------|
| Main Controller | `al` | Manages the complete active learning cycle |
| Samplers | `Sampler` | Various sampling strategies for new points |
| Model Trainers | `ml_model_trainer` | Handles ML model training |
| Uncertainty Quantification | `uq` methods | Evaluates model uncertainty |

**Active Learning Process Flow**
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["Start Active Learning"] --> INIT["Initial Data Sampling<br/>get_initial_data_pool()"]
    INIT --> LABEL1["Label Initial Points<br/>label_points()"]
    LABEL1 --> TRAIN["Train ML Model<br/>create_ml_model()"]
    TRAIN --> SAMPLE["Sample New Points<br/>use_ml_model()"]
    SAMPLE --> UNCERTAIN{"Points Above<br/>UQ Threshold?"}
    UNCERTAIN -->|Yes| LABEL2["Label New Points<br/>label_points()"]
    UNCERTAIN -->|No| CONVERGED["AL Converged"]
    LABEL2 --> UPDATE["Update Training Set"]
    UPDATE --> RETRAIN["Retrain Model<br/>create_ml_model()"]
    RETRAIN --> SAMPLE
    
    subgraph "Sampling Methods"
        WIGNER["Wigner Sampling"]
        MD["Molecular Dynamics"]
        GEOMOPT["Geometry Optimization"]
        NAMD["Surface Hopping MD"]
    end
    
    SAMPLE --> WIGNER
    SAMPLE --> MD  
    SAMPLE --> GEOMOPT
    SAMPLE --> NAMD
```

Sources: [mlatom/al.py:355-403](), [mlatom/al.py:414-584](), [mlatom/al_utils.py:8-757]()

### Sampling Strategies

The `Sampler` class provides multiple strategies for generating candidate points:

| Sampler | Method | Use Case |
|---------|--------|----------|
| `wigner` | Quantum harmonic oscillator sampling | Initial conditions generation |
| `md` | Molecular dynamics trajectories | Dynamic sampling |
| `batch_md` | Parallel MD trajectories | High-throughput sampling |
| `geomopt` | Geometry optimization paths | Transition state searches |
| `lzsh` | Landau-Zener surface hopping | Nonadiabatic dynamics |

The samplers are implemented with a common interface in [mlatom/al_utils.py:34-35]():

```python
def sample(self,**kwargs):
    return self.sampler_function(**kwargs)
```

Sources: [mlatom/al_utils.py:8-33](), [mlatom/al_utils.py:83-123](), [mlatom/al_utils.py:167-243]()

## Neural Network Models

The neural network models are primarily based on the ANI (Accurate Neural Network Interatomic potentials) architecture, interfaced through TorchANI.

### ANI Model Implementation

The `ani` class provides a complete interface to TorchANI for training and prediction:

**ANI Model Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ANI Model Components"
        AEV["AEV Computer<br/>Atomic Environment Vectors"]
        NN["Neural Networks<br/>Species-specific networks"]
        ENERGY["Energy Prediction"]
        FORCES["Force Calculation<br/>-∇E"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Variants"
        ANI1X["ANI-1x<br/>Pre-trained"]
        ANI1CCX["ANI-1ccx<br/>Coupled-cluster trained"]
        ANI2X["ANI-2x<br/>Extended training"]
        CUSTOM["Custom Models<br/>User-trained"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Infrastructure"
        HYPERPARAMS["Hyperparameters<br/>Learning rates, batch size"]
        OPTIMIZERS["Optimizers<br/>AdamW + SGD"]
        SCHEDULERS["LR Schedulers<br/>ReduceLROnPlateau"]
    end
    
    AEV --> NN
    NN --> ENERGY
    ENERGY --> FORCES
    
    HYPERPARAMS --> OPTIMIZERS
    OPTIMIZERS --> SCHEDULERS
```

Sources: [mlatom/interfaces/torchani_interface.py:86-139](), [mlatom/interfaces/torchani_interface.py:277-305]()

### Key Features

The ANI implementation includes:

- **Hyperparameter Management**: Comprehensive hyperparameter system with optimization support [mlatom/interfaces/torchani_interface.py:99-127]()
- **Multi-GPU Support**: CUDA device management and batch processing [mlatom/interfaces/torchani_interface.py:140-159]()
- **Energy and Force Training**: Joint training on energies and gradients [mlatom/interfaces/torchani_interface.py:495-520]()
- **Model Loading/Saving**: Checkpoint management and model persistence [mlatom/interfaces/torchani_interface.py:175-276]()

### Training Process

The training process supports validation monitoring and early stopping:

```python
# Key training parameters from hyperparameters
batch_size = 8
max_epochs = 1000000
learning_rate = 0.001
early_stopping_learning_rate = 1.0E-5
force_coefficient = 0.1
```

Sources: [mlatom/interfaces/torchani_interface.py:308-544]()

## AI-Enhanced Quantum Methods

The AI-enhanced methods combine neural networks with quantum mechanical corrections to achieve high accuracy for molecular properties.

### AIQM1 Method

AIQM1 combines ANI neural networks with quantum mechanical corrections:

**AIQM1 Composition Structure**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "AIQM1 Components"
        ANI_NN["8 ANI Neural Networks<br/>ani_nns_in_aiqm1"]
        ATOMIC_SHIFT["Atomic Energy Shifts<br/>atomic_energy_shift"]
        ODM2["ODM2* Method<br/>Quantum corrections"]
        D4["D4 Dispersion<br/>wb97x functional"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Tree Structure"
        ROOT["aiqm1_model<br/>model_tree_node"]
        AVG["Average Operation<br/>operator='average'"]
        SUM["Sum Operation<br/>operator='sum'"]
    end
    
    ANI_NN --> AVG
    AVG --> SUM
    ATOMIC_SHIFT --> SUM
    ODM2 --> SUM
    D4 --> SUM
    SUM --> ROOT
    
    subgraph "Supported Methods"
        AIQM1_BASE["AIQM1<br/>Base method"]
        AIQM1_DFT["AIQM1@DFT<br/>DFT reference"]
        AIQM1_DFTS["AIQM1@DFT*<br/>No dispersion"]
    end
```

Sources: [mlatom/aiqm1.py:48-66](), [mlatom/aiqm1.py:171-276]()

### AIQM2 Method

AIQM2 uses GFN2-xTB* as the base quantum method:

| Component | Purpose | Implementation |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| `gfn2xtbstar` | Base quantum method | GFN2-xTB* interface |
| `aiqm2_nn` | ML corrections | 8 ANI models averaged |
| `d4wb97x` | Dispersion corrections | D4 with wb97x functional |

The model composition follows the same tree structure as AIQM1 but with different base methods [mlatom/aiqm2.py:122-164]().

### Model Tree Composition

Both AIQM methods use the `model_tree_node` system for composing multiple models:

```python
# Example composition operators
operator='predict'    # Apply model prediction
operator='average'     # Average multiple predictions  
operator='sum'        # Sum contributions
operator='weighted_sum' # Weighted combination
```

This allows flexible combination of different theoretical methods and ML models [mlatom/model_cls.py:953-1077]().

Sources: [mlatom/aiqm1.py:15-132](), [mlatom/aiqm2.py:5-165](), [mlatom/model_cls.py:953-1135]()

## Model Framework and Base Classes

The ML system is built on a hierarchy of base classes that provide common functionality:

**Model Class Hierarchy**
```mermaid
graph TB
    MODEL["model<br/>(model_cls.py)"] --> ML_MODEL["ml_model<br/>Training capabilities"]
    MODEL --> TORCH_MODEL["torch_model<br/>PyTorch integration"]
    MODEL --> METHOD_MODEL["method_model<br/>QM method interface"]
    
    TORCH_MODEL --> TORCHANI_MODEL["torchani_model<br/>TorchANI specific"]
    
    ML_MODEL --> ANI_CLASS["ani<br/>(torchani_interface.py)"]
    TORCHANI_MODEL --> ANI_CLASS
    TORCHANI_MODEL --> AIQM1_CLASS["aiqm1<br/>(aiqm1.py)"]
    METHOD_MODEL --> AIQM1_CLASS
    METHOD_MODEL --> AIQM2_CLASS["aiqm2<br/>(aiqm2.py)"]
    
    MODEL --> DOWNLOADABLE["downloadable_model<br/>Auto-download models"]
    DOWNLOADABLE --> AIQM1_CLASS
    DOWNLOADABLE --> AIQM2_CLASS
```

### Key Base Class Features

| Base Class | Key Features | File Reference |
|------------|--------------|----------------|
| `model` | Thread management, prediction interface | [model_cls.py:20-131]() |
| `ml_model` | Training, validation, hyperparameter optimization | [model_cls.py:336-847]() |
| `torch_model` | PyTorch thread configuration | [model_cls.py:132-144]() |
| `downloadable_model` | Automatic model downloading | [model_cls.py:201-334]() |

### Hyperparameter System

The framework includes a sophisticated hyperparameter management system:

```python
class hyperparameters(UserDict):
    # Auto-converts values to hyperparameter objects
    # Supports optimization spaces: 'linear', 'log'
    # Includes validation and type casting
```

Hyperparameter optimization supports multiple algorithms including grid search, TPE (Tree-structured Parzen Estimator), and scipy optimizers [mlatom/model_cls.py:602-721]().

Sources: [mlatom/model_cls.py:20-952](), [mlatom/model_cls.py:849-951]()
